deliveries.description: Deliveries is every delivery system some tuner of this board reaches.

location.description:
Location is the bus and address. Not part of the name: the kernel reassigns
it.

name.description: Name is what the board is known by; its tuners' names are built on it.

naming.description:
Naming says what the name was built from, and Stable whether it survives the
board being unplugged and put back into the same socket.

open.description: Open is whether the daemon is holding the board open right now.

probe_error.description:
ProbeError says why an ?open=1 listing could not confirm this board. Empty
when nothing was tried or nothing went wrong, so an unconfirmed answer never
passes for a confirmed one.

probed.description:
Probed reports whether the tuners below were read from the hardware. False
means they were worked out from the board's identifiers, which is the
default: opening a board powers it up and loads firmware, and listing is not
a request to do that.

present.description:
Present is filled in only when the slot was looked at, which means opening
the board.

atr.description: ATR is the card's answer to reset, which is what identifies it.

max_input.description:
MaxInput is the longest command APDU this reader carries, the paths behind it
moving one T=1 block per message.

protocol.description: Protocol is what the reader and the card agreed on; these speak T=1 only.

released.description:
Released reports whether this connection was holding what it asked to give up.
A false is not a failure: a client tidying up may ask twice.

apdus.description: APDUs are command APDUs in hexadecimal; separators are ignored.

changed.description:
Changed says whether the count moved while this request waited, as against the
wait running out.

events.description:
Events counts the insertions and removals this slot has seen. A client passes
the last one it knows as `since` and is answered when the count moves.

sharing.description:
Sharing is how many connections hold the card, or -1 when one holds it
exclusively.

apdu.description: APDU is one command in hexadecimal; separators are ignored.

status.description: Status is the two trailing status bytes.

hostapi.Controls.description:
Controls is what a channel may set on this tuner beside the channel: the
supply on its lead (lnb_power) and its gain. Known from the model, so it is
there before the board is opened. Absent where there is nothing to set --
which is what tells a client not to offer it.

status.description: Status is the two trailing status bytes.

hostapi.GainControl.description: Gain is present where gain is honoured.

decibels.description: Decibels is the steps, least first, for kind "steps".

deliveries.description:
Deliveries narrows the setting to these systems, where the amplifier sits on
one input only. Absent means every system the tuner tunes.

kind.description:
Kind is "switch" for an amplifier that is in or out (min, max, auto) and
"steps" for one with levels, which a gain in dB is matched to.

hostapi.LNBControl.description: LNB is present where lnb_power is honoured.

levels.description:
Levels is what lnb_power accepts here: "off" where the supply can be
switched off, then "low" and "high".

low.description:
Low and High are what the two levels are worth ("11V", "15V"), absent for a
supply that is only on or off.

shared.description: Shared is "board" or "card" where one supply feeds more than this tuner.

reason.description: Reason narrows a code that covers more than one situation.

hostapi.StreamCounts.description: Stream is what the multiplex looked like on the way out, while streaming.

bytes.description:
Bytes is everything the tuner produced; Packets is what was recognised as a
packet, stuffing included; Skipped is bytes outside any packet.

control.description:
Control is the TLV signalling that describes the multiplex, and IPv4, IPv6 and
CompressedIP how the datagrams inside are carried. TLV only.

discontinuities.description:
Discontinuities is packets that did not follow the last one in their own run
-- a TS continuity counter within a PID, or an MMTP sequence number within a
packet identifier. Missing data, not damaged data.

errors.description: Errors is packets the demodulator marked as uncorrectable. TS only.

forgotten.description:
Forgotten counts times the sequence table was emptied because more runs
appeared at once than any multiplex has. Anything but zero means the stream
is being read as something it is not, and Discontinuities beside it cannot
be believed.

format.description:
Format is which multiplex this was read as, "ts" or "tlv". It decides which
fields below are filled in.

nulls.description:
Nulls is stuffing. A multiplex that is almost all stuffing is one whose
services are not arriving.

scrambled.description: Scrambled is packets still carrying their scrambling bits. TS only.

sync_losses.description: SyncLosses counts breaks in packet-boundary alignment, not packets.

undecodable.description: Undecodable is TLV packets whose MMTP header could not be reached. TLV only.

hostapi.TuneResult.description:
Status carries whatever was measured before the request failed, so a scan
still gets the signal strength of a frequency that did not lock.

ignored.description:
Ignored names properties left out of the tuning because they describe what a
multiplex carries rather than how to receive it, so a caller pasting in a
channel-file section can see what was not used.

relative_streams.description:
RelativeStreams is how many places a satellite transponder's table holds,
for a driver that names a stream by its place rather than by its identifier.
The Earthsoft character devices read the transmission control block
themselves and take an index into it -- the numbering recpt1 writes as
BS01_1 -- so a caller holding identifiers from a network table needs this
count to translate them.

dropped.description:
Dropped is transport packets thrown away because the reader could not keep up.
It separates a recording that lost data from one fed a poor signal.

locked.description:
The rest is filled in only while the tuner is in use: reading it means talking
to the hardware.

mode.description:
Mode is a hardware setting beside the channel, where the tuner has one: a TBS
card's demodulator mode, shared by the whole card. Absent for most tuners.

priority.description:
Priority is how much the work holding this tuner said it mattered, as its
X-Coax-Priority header gave it. Absent for a tuner nobody holds: zero is a
real priority, so "nobody holds it" cannot be spelled as zero.

settings.description: Settings is what a driver measured, not what it was asked for.

tuned.description:
Tuned is the channel the tuner is set to, as the properties the tune took --
what was asked for. Absent for a tuner nobody holds or one not yet tuned.

arch.description:
Arch is the processor the build is for (GOARCH: amd64, arm64), so that a
client can say which binary is running beside which it has on disk.

started.description: Started lets a client tell a daemon it just launched from one already running.

info.description:
The tuner daemon's interface. One process owns the hardware and hands out what it receives; this is how everything else asks.
This number is the description's own: its last part moves when something is added that an existing client can ignore, and its first when a shape an existing client reads changes out from under it. It is not the daemon's version, which is what GET /version reports.
A daemon that does not know a parameter refuses the whole request rather than ignoring it, so a client sends only what is described here.
info.title: coaxd

A zero `wait` answers at once with the state as it stands.

get.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document for everything here, generated from the handlers and the shapes they answer with.

The endpoint everything else exists for. Takes the same parameters as /tune and then streams what the tuner receives, chunked, until the connection closes or a bound is reached.

**The connection is the lease.** The tuner is held for as long as the connection is open and given back when it closes, however it closes -- so a client that vanishes does not strand hardware.

Unless `sync=off`, the first part of the stream is checked for transport or TLV framing before anything is sent, and a tuner locked to noise is refused rather than recorded in silence.

get.description:
Takes a tuner, tunes it, waits for a lock and answers what it found. **It does not return the transport stream**; it is what a scan uses to ask whether a channel is there.

Case decides what a parameter is. A name in capitals is a channel-file property, passed through exactly as written, so a section of a channel file can be handed over as it stands. A name in lower case is a shorthand or one of the controls, and an unknown one in lower case is refused rather than ignored.

get.description:
Every board and the tuners on it.

Nothing is opened unless asked for. Opening a board powers it and on some models loads firmware, which is not a reasonable thing to do to answer a question about what is plugged in -- so the configuration is answered from what each backend knows about the model, and marked `probed: false`. With `open=1` each board is really opened and the answer is marked `probed: true`.

parameters.description: open each board to confirm what is on it
parameters.name: open

get.description:
Lock, carrier-to-noise, input level, quality and dropped packets, plus the statistics of the multiplex leaving it when it is streaming.

It may be asked while the tuner is streaming; that is what it is for. A tuner that is not streaming has no `stream` key at all rather than one full of zeroes, because "saw no packets" and "saw no broken packets" are opposite answers.
